q: the center admin pulls me aside as I am dropping my daughter off. She tells me my daugher's refusal to nap is becoming an issue, especially since she can be loud, disruptive, and refuses to say quiet/laying down. Naptime is when they do breaks and they don't have the headcount for her to have one on one time.
cx: Mother of a two-year-old who will not nap at daycare.

q: I feel like it's *my fault* that my kid won't nap. Like it's some moral failing on my part as a mom because she can't settle in.
cx: Same mother, writing near 1am.

q: It's also about getting my husband on board, too, with the changes. He's a creature of rigid habits
cx: Changing bedtime needs the other parent too.

q: Sleep consultants will make random changes to just get over their 2-week period but after that you will be on your own and then you will be winging it, after paying hundreds of dollars to someone to just tell you to do either “sit besides crib” or “cry it out”.
cx: Parent who went through a consultant's programme for a 7-month-old; title: it's more about luck.

q: Most sleep consultants are just winging it with their set programs for parents and they make random changes to the plan when parents give feedback about it not working
cx: Same parent after talking with 15 to 20 other parents.

q: It just feels like there’s a big psyop going on here in the US, and some capitalistic roots that this entire thing about sleep training and preying on new parents’ sleep deprivation turned into a full blown industry. It’s easy for sleep consultants to get on a call for a few minutes and tell you that it’s okay if your baby cried for 90 minutes straight, every single night.
cx: Same post.

q: those who got lucky make all the noise about sleep training being the best thing since sliced bread but for those it didn’t, don’t talk about it because they feel like failures.
cx: Why success stories dominate, in this parent's view.

q: I'm a teacher so when I went to work my baby went to my mother in laws.. where she held her and rocked her to sleep. And I was so tired and baby wouldn't sleep so we started doing that too.
cx: First-time mother of an 11-month-old, starting training on summer break.

q: We are trying the chair method where we sit in the room with her but dont hold her. If we leave the room she becomes hysterical. And when she finally goes to sleep, starting around midnight she'll wake every 45 minutes to an hour for the rest of the night.
cx: Same mother, first week of the chair method.

q: I am a new first time mum and I feel like I’m DROWNING in my babys sleep schedule. I want to do gentle sleep trainjng. Strictly no cry it out (I’m an early childhood teacher with a masters in early childhood development and I’m VERY against this so please don’t recommend to me).
cx: Mother of a 5-month-old who now wakes every 2-3 hours.

q: Wake windows aim to be 2/2/2.5 but they keep varying due to his naps. He’s on 2-3 naps. […] I would allow him to go past the 2 hour mark if the morning nap was short and he had a bad nights sleep to clear some sleep debt but now I feel ljke I’m trapped in a weird cycle.
cx: Same mother doing the nap arithmetic.

q: I downloaded the Huckelberry app to help with wake windows and the sweet spot and so far it’s been spot on however the issue lies with his multiple wakings
cx: The app helps with naps, not with nights.

q: To start off I know a lot of people sleep train, I just don’t think that’s right for my family or for my little guy. […] I chalk a lot of his bad sleep up to the fact that he is just an active sensitive kid.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 1-year-old who has never slept well.

q: Then she went on the say that I should sleep train and have you tried laying him down drowsy but awake. YES OF COURSE I HAVE TRIED THIS!!!!
cx: At the one-year check-up, after she said she was not keen on sleep training.

q: I feel totally defeated and just need some encouragement that sleep will get better. […] I haven’t slept through the night in a year.
cx: Her ask is a pep talk.

q: they've been bouncing him on a yoga ball to go back to sleep, which we think has started to unravel his sleep training at night and on weekends. We were told by one worker, in an agitated way, that he's the only baby they've seen who is sleep trained.
cx: Mother of a sleep-trained 8-month-old, five weeks into daycare.

q: it just seems like they are frustrated by him, want explicit instructions for what to do that will "work" (hell, I'm mostly winging it anyways!) and then otherwise don't really care to fix it.
cx: The daycare wants a written method she does not have.

q: I get their constraints and I'm trying to work with them, but I'm also a working parent and just human with needs in general and need that baby to sleep at night!!
cx: After her comment was downvoted.

q: He is napping very little during his time there, despite making great progress on this at home with independent napping the past month. […] Due to the lessened daytime sleep, I've followed advice to move bedtime up for him.
cx: Parent of a 4-month-old in the first week of daycare.

q: If I’m not home she’ll go down in 10 minutes for Dad and sleep longer stretches, she literally sleeps better when he puts her down but if I’m home she’ll go into full meltdowns
cx: Mother of a 13-month-old; shift work and placements mean Dad covers some nights.

q: why won’t she pick Dad? Why does she sleep so well with him when I’m not here? WTF do we do to share the load?
cx: Same mother; they will not sleep train.

q: We have considered me just leaving the house while he puts her down, he just gets overwhelmed so I feel guilty walking away, might be time I toughen up and say too bad
cx: After a blunt commenter's reply.

q: I am a shell of a human from sleep deprivation, returning to work and trying to finish my degree
cx: Same mother.

q: I am dreading the next day at daycare. I sent them a message explaining his wake windows, sleepy cues etc. He's very alert and sensitive to stimuli, so I feel he has a hard time switching off when they put him down.
cx: Parent of a 4-month-old who naps well at home.

q: At home we’re also dealing with a lot of tantrums, whining, and bedtime refusal, so it’s definitely not just a daycare thing at this point.
cx: Pregnant mother of a 25-month-old whose days fell apart after an illness.

q: Why won’t my kid nap at home? Daycare says he naps from roughly 12-2 every day. […] The last three weekends we have not been able to get him to nap at home. We keep his sleep and eating schedule the same as it is on weekdays.
cx: Parent of a 14-month-old with weekends alone ahead.

q: Please help me. I am so tired. I also miss having even just an hour to myself during the day.
cx: Same parent.

q: If you did NOT sleep train your baby, did they eventually just start sleeping through the night on their own? Or are you still sharing a bed with your five year old? What happened and what do your nights actually look like now?
cx: Parent of a 10-month-old waking at least four times a night since the 4-month regression.

q: I tried the Ferber method once and it did not work for us at all. Supposedly they are supposed to stop crying eventually, even if it takes a long time—and yea, no, that’s not what happened for us at all. He just cried and cried until he became completely hysterical.

q: We were both extremely traumatized. I was crying. I still cry when I think about it. This is all to say I don’t think I have it in me to sleep train.
cx: Why she will not try again.

q: We have no village, no grandparents or friends or relatives who live close by. Financially things are tight right now so as much as I’d like to hire a night nurse that won’t be possible.
cx: Husband is a one-person business working long hours.

q: Omg, you just described my son. 😭 he also takes 4 bottles a night. I will definitely be buying this book
cx: A commenter's book recommendation, bought on recognition.

q: it got to a point where 95% of posts I was seeing from that community were basically “you are an evil, abusive parent if you sleep train” — so I just felt like, if I can’t make cosleeping work, and sleep training is abuse, then where do I go from here…
cx: On leaving an anti-sleep-training community.

q: Every time I see someone say their baby just started sleeping through the night in 12 hour stretches, on their own, at like 3 months old — my stomach literally drops. 😭 I feel like I’m living a completely different experience from every other parent, or else I’m just extremely bad at this.
cx: After reading replies from non-trainers with easy sleepers.

q: He has not outgrown nap because he takes naps fine at daycare during the week. […] Does anyone have actionable advice for making weekend naps happen? Or at least some moral support, because my partner and I are really exhausted.

q: We tried for the past 5 days for my husband to take our newborn for 3 hours (10-1:30ish am) so I could get a stretch of sleep […] Mainly because the baby wouldnt sleep at all with him, just kept going through pumped bottles and would still be wide awake for hours.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a 2-week-old and an almost-3-year-old.

q: I dont know how I can ask my husband for more help so I can get sleep. He takes on so much with our toddler and I feel guilty I’m not spending as much time with him. But the night time is really killing me

q: at home prior to daycare (and on weekends currently) he had barely been making 2 hours wake time. […] He's only been there for two weeks but he will commonly go 3 hours without napping.

q: I don't want to micromanage because these people are professionals and have taken care of a lot more babies, when this is my first kid.
cx: Why she hesitates to push the daycare.
